Once the address is created I'll have to correctly fund it with a tx consisting of 2 inputs:
VOUT 0 must be the inscription
VOUT 1 must be the fees


The ord is located at (can be found via ord --testnet4 wallet inscriptions):
"location": "7b59080b7a7b2db9966c202ae64f9be6c781d2e26f5191b1592e69bc6a4ede48:0:0",
wich means at vout=0

Always make sure about the amount that an ord contains, (the ord was inscribed on 1000 sats)
can do that via:
ord --testnet4 wallet outputs

------------------------VARIABLES TO SET + command -----------
ESCROW_ADDR="tb1qp5val0gv97z5sgz908fq7ckm67x6apzy2h7sk8a8dp2539fg3fcqwczy8y"
INSCR_TXID="7b59080b7a7b2db9966c202ae64f9be6c781d2e26f5191b1592e69bc6a4ede48"
INSCR_VOUT=0
INSCR_AMT_BTC="0.00010000"
FEE_TXID="6d9440829a80cf7239b6fbe7fbdd8f96c835912a7061db146ac1273cd78077a5"
FEE_VOUT=1

new address to get the change of the fee
CHANGE_ADDR=$(bitcoin-cli getrawchangeaddress bech32m) 
echo "CHANGE_ADDR=$CHANGE_ADDR"
CHANGE_ADDR=tb1pyf5snju2p83efh5m8qmunxyrvd9zgnj2ng809tqdsc05pwrsuuvspv8shq


PSBT=$(bitcoin-cli walletcreatefundedpsbt \ 
  "[{\"txid\":\"$INSCR_TXID\",\"vout\":$INSCR_VOUT},{\"txid\":\"$FEE_TXID\",\"vout\":$FEE_VOUT}]" \
  "[{\"$ESCROW_ADDR\":$INSCR_AMT_BTC}]" \
  0 \
  "{\"add_inputs\":false,\"changeAddress\":\"$CHANGE_ADDR\",\"changePosition\":1,\"fee_rate\":5,\"lockUnspents\":true}" \
  | jq -r .psbt)

echo "PSBT=$PSBT"



double check the psbt with:

bitcoin-cli decodepsbt "$PSBT" | jq '{vin: .tx.vin, vout: .tx.vout}'

sign and finalize with :

SIGNED_PSBT=$(bitcoin-cli  walletprocesspsbt "$PSBT" | jq -r .psbt)
FINAL_HEX=$(bitcoin-cli  finalizepsbt "$SIGNED_PSBT" true | jq -r .hex)
echo "FINAL_HEX=$FINAL_HEX"

then check if the tx would be accepted: (in the output seek for "allowed":true)

bitcoin-cli testmempoolaccept "[\"$FINAL_HEX\"]"


broadcast:

ESCROW_FUND_TXID=$(bitcoin-cli sendrawtransaction "$FINAL_HEX")
echo "Escrow funded in tx: $ESCROW_FUND_TXID"

Escrow funded in tx: 3780e7bb43ae7d72eba20c7c6a57c685f2eb79f28ec6cbac45c08d7e0c003922


now the p2wsh is ready for the buyer to redeem.


TO redeem the p2wsh we need two steps:
build the psbt with ordinal_buyer_claim_p1 and finalize it with p2
THE FLOW IS::
1. run script p1
2. run bitcoin-cli --rpcwallet="buyer_wallet" walletprocesspsbt "$PSBT" | jq -r .psbt , save it to a variable and put the signed output in the p2 script 
3. run script p2
4.extract and broadcast


IMPORTANT NOTE : THE ONE WHO OWNS THE CHANGE (the taproot founder) must sign the tx at point 2.
in practice:
1. PSBT=$(node ordinal_buyer_claim_p1.js)
2. PSBT_CORE=$(bitcoin-cli --rpcwallet="buyer_wallet" walletprocesspsbt "$PSBT" | jq -r .psbt)
3. echo it and put it in p2
4. PSBT_FINAL=$(node ordinal_buyer_claim_p2.js)
FINAL_HEX=$(bitcoin-cli --rpcwallet="buyer_wallet" finalizepsbt "$PSBT_FINAL" true | jq -r .hex)

TO TEST ACCEPTANCE:
bitcoin-cli testmempoolaccept "[\"$FINAL_HEX\"]"

TO BROADCAST:
bitcoin-cli sendrawtransaction "$FINAL_HEX"

------------------------------------------------------------------ RUN 2
INSC ID 7b59080b7a7b2db9966c202ae64f9be6c781d2e26f5191b1592e69bc6a4ede48i0

In this first run there was a bit of a problem with the fees,
the last psbt needed the signature of the seller, in order to unlock the seller fees to the p2wsh.

In this second run I'll be moving the ord from "buyer" to "buyer_wallet",
so that the buyer_wallet will pay the fees and unlock the p2wsh on its own.

tb1pnjydaah9cda5ralsc599kl47tmf9mrs59yes0mqpr74zfr8fqxnsasgyw9


THEN I BUILD IT WITH:

PSBT=$(bitcoin-cli -rpcwallet=buyer walletcreatefundedpsbt \
  "[{\"txid\":\"$INSCR_TXID\",\"vout\":$INSCR_VOUT},{\"txid\":\"$FEE_TXID\",\"vout\":$FEE_VOUT}]" \
  "[{\"$ESCROW_ADDR\":0.00010000}]" \
  0 \
  "{\"add_inputs\":false,\"changeAddress\":\"$CHANGE_ADDR\",\"changePosition\":1,\"fee_rate\":5,\"lockUnspents\":true}" \
  | jq -r .psbt)

Then same as before :
PSBT_SIGNED=$(bitcoin-cli -rpcwallet=buyer walletprocesspsbt "$PSBT" | jq -r .psbt)
FUND_HEX=$(bitcoin-cli finalizepsbt "$PSBT_SIGNED" true | jq -r .hex)
FUND_TXID=$(bitcoin-cli sendrawtransaction "$FUND_HEX")

------------- Now the contract is defined and we switch to the buyer side ---------------------

I've also created a witness script decoder so that we can know the details of the "contract" from the hex itself.
decode_witness_script.js

then the buyer with the needed info will build a partially signed tx:

node buyer_redeem_v2.js 


Then we process it with wallet :
PSBT_CORE=$(bitcoin-cli -rpcwallet=buyer_wallet walletprocesspsbt "$BUYER_PSBT" | jq -r .psbt)

TO CHECK IT : bitcoin-cli  decodepsbt "$PSBT_CORE" | jq '.inputs[1]' 


THEN WE USE THIS AND PASTE ALL THE INFO INSIDE THE ordinal_buyer_claim_p2 (finalizer)

Sometimes it is useful to save this output into a file : node ordinal_buyer_claim_p2 > finalpsbt.b64
In this way we don't get strange errors


THE OUTPUT IS :

%       


FINAL_HEX=$(bitcoin-cli finalizepsbt "$(cat psbtfinal.b64)" true | jq -r .hex) 
echo "$FINAL_HEX"




Then we test the acceptance:

bitcoin-cli testmempoolaccept "[\"$FINAL_HEX\"]"

And finally we broadcast it :

REDEEM_TXID=$(bitcoin-cli sendrawtransaction "$FINAL_HEX")
echo "REDEEM_TXID=$REDEEM_TXID"

REDEEM_TXID=b84ec7b8e9f28b0f2c99e477ee141ff073365356d0865cbeb2a5f8e0e13e95c4
